prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim. Injury: whiplash. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1416; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Reviewed the first notice of loss for the left-turn collision. Insured reports the other vehicle struck the rear quarter panel while the insured was completing a left turn at an intersection. Both drivers reported as ambulatory at scene. Claimant states neck pain and stiffness and has not yet retained counsel. Photos requested from insured.

Entry 2: Spoke with the claimant by phone. Claimant describes whiplash symptoms including neck stiffness, headache, and limited rotation to the right. Claimant confirmed no attorney is handling the matter. Explained the claims process and requested the names of any treating providers and copies of medical records once available.

Entry 3: Received the police report for the intersection collision. Report notes the other driver was proceeding straight through on a green signal. Insured's account is consistent with a left turn across oncoming traffic. Liability appears to lean toward the insured, pending review of the scene photos and any witness statements.

Entry 4: Claimant submitted a treatment summary from an urgent care visit following the collision, listing a diagnosis of cervical strain consistent with whiplash. Claimant plans to continue physical therapy for several weeks. Requested itemized bills and a current status update on symptoms. No settlement discussion has taken place as claimant remains unrepresented.

Entry 5: Completed a review of the file. Liability assessment remains probable against the insured. Medical documentation is being gathered to evaluate the whiplash injury. Scheduled a follow-up call with the claimant to confirm receipt of records and discuss next steps. Reserve reviewed and will be adjusted once the treatment plan is clearer.
